mc.prompt: In an early-pregnancy model, hCG cannot act on the corpus luteum. Which consequence is most directly predicted?
mc.answer: Reduced corpus-luteum hormone support for the endometrium
mc.explanation: Without the supporting signal, luteal hormone production may decline, affecting the lining.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.
options: Reduced corpus-luteum hormone support for the endometrium
Direct conversion of progesterone into sperm
An LH surge caused by increased milk secretion

mc.prompt: Which conclusion is not established by detecting hCG alone?
mc.answer: That implantation is definitely in the normal uterine location
mc.explanation: A hormone test is not an anatomical image and does not establish implantation location.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.
options: That the tested sample contains detectable hCG
That implantation is definitely in the normal uterine location
That hCG is being used as a pregnancy-associated signal
That the measurement concerns a hormone rather than chromosome number

writing.prompt: Trace the role of hCG in maintaining the endometrium. Include the hormone’s source, its direct target and the next hormones in the chain.
writing.model: Trophoblast-derived tissue releases hCG. hCG maintains the ovarian corpus luteum, which continues secreting progesterone and estrogen. These hormones support the endometrium and help prevent the normal menstrual shedding associated with falling ovarian hormones.
criteria: Identifies the relevant structures or quantities.

Uses the stated evidence and avoids a stronger conclusion than it supports.

writing.prompt: Explain why a decline in hCG after its early peak need not mean a loss of all progesterone support.
writing.model: The placenta increasingly produces progesterone and estrogen during the first trimester. The hormonal source changes over development, so progesterone can remain supported even when hCG falls from an earlier peak.
criteria: Identifies the relevant structures or quantities.

mc.prompt: Which pair shares an ectodermal origin?
mc.explanation: Ectoderm contributes both outer epidermis and nervous tissue.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.

mc.prompt: Why is “the entire digestive system comes from endoderm” too broad?
mc.answer: Digestive organs include muscle and connective tissue with other germ-layer origins
mc.explanation: Endoderm contributes important linings and glandular tissues, not every tissue in the organ.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.
options: Germ layers appear only after birth
Endoderm never contributes to the digestive system
Every digestive cell has a unique genome
Digestive organs include muscle and connective tissue with other germ-layer origins

writing.prompt: Explain what gastrulation changes and identify the three layers it establishes.
writing.model: Gastrulation reorganizes embryonic cells through movement and produces ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm. Each layer contributes to particular tissue lineages as development continues. This is a change in organization and developmental pathways, not just an increase in cell number.
criteria: Identifies the relevant structures or quantities.
Explains the causal relationship or calculation, not just the final result.
Uses the stated evidence and avoids a stronger conclusion than it supports.

writing.prompt: A damaged developmental process affects intestinal muscle but not its epithelial lining. Explain why the two tissues need not share the same germ-layer origin.
writing.model: Intestinal smooth muscle is a mesodermal derivative, whereas much of the intestinal epithelial lining is endodermal. One organ contains several tissue types, so a change can affect one developmental contribution without identically affecting the other.
criteria: Identifies the relevant structures or quantities.
